Present appeal has been filed by the claimants seeking enhancement of compensation of Rs.12,15,000 Rs 12,15,000/- granted by Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Patiala (hereinafter referred to as "the learned Tribunal") vide Award dated 10.02.2016 passed in MAC Case No.20/21.07.2015 20/21.07.2015 filed under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act") Act").

The 4 claimants are the: i) widow; ii) 19-year-old daughter; iii) 18-year year-old son; iv) 16-year-old minor son of the deceased-Sucha Singh who was 53 years old at the time of accident.
2. Brief facts of the case are that the learned Tribunal on the basis of pleadings and evidence adduced before it concluded that deceased-Sucha Sucha Singh had died in a motor vehicular accident that took place on 18.05.2015 18.05.2 due to rash and negligent driving of motorcycle 1 of 6 Neutral Citation No:=2025:PHHC:000693 bearing registration No.PB-11-BP-8364 No. (hereinafter referred to as 'the offending vehicle'), being owned and driven by respondent No.1 and insured by respondent No.2.
No. . Learned Tribunal awarded compensation as above along with interest @ 6% % per annum from the date of filing the claim petition till actual realisation.

The amount of compensation is apportioned amongst the claimants as under: -

It is submitted that the deceased was working as a Ragi in the Gurdwara Sahib and was earning at least Rs.20,000/ Rs.20,000/- per month.

4. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.2/Insurance Company Compan submits that there is no evidence whatsoever adduced on record by the appellants to prove that the deceased was working as a Ragi in the Gurdwara Sahib.
As such, notional income of the deceased has been rightly assessed by the learned Tribunal as 10,000/- per month..
It is very fairly admitted that the claimants are entitled to future prospects in conformity with the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Pranay Sethi (supra).
It is further pointed out that the claimant No.1 has been awarded Rs.1 lakh as loss of consortium.
It is accordingly prayed that no ground for enhancement is made out except for grant of future prospects.

6. I have heard learned counsel for the parties.

3 of 6 Neutral Citation No:=2025:PHHC:000693 7. It has been argued ued on behalf of the appellants that the learned Tribunal has wrongly assessed income of the deceased as only Rs.10,000/-- per month; whereas it was the pleaded case of the appellants before the learned Tribunal that the deceased was earning Rs.20,000/-- per month by working as Ragi in the Gurdwara Sahib.

However, a perusal of the impugned Award shows that in Para 21 thereof, it has been recorded as follows:-
follows:
"21.

Although according to the claimants, the deceased was serving as Granthi in a Gurudwara and also working as Ragi participating in religious ceremonies and in that way was earning Rs.20,000/-per per month. PW1 Kamaljit Kaur widow of the deceased in her cross-examination examination has stated that she has not any documentary evidence proof fro from the SGPC or from any Gurudwara Committee that her husband was working as Ragi or Granti in the Gurudwara.
She further stated that she has not brought any certificate to the effect that her husband was working as Ragi as well as Grant Granthi in the Gurudwara Sahib.
ahib. However, admittedly the deceased was not an income tax payee."
8. Learned counsel for the appellants is unable to dispute the above said findings of the learned Tribunal.
Even nothing has been shown to this Court to remotely indicate that the deceased was working as a Ragi or Granthi in the Gurdwara Sahib let alone any d documentary evidence in support.

As such, Learned Tribunal has correctly held that "...in the State of Punjab even a casual labourer manage to earn Rs.250/ 4 of 6 Neutral Citation No:=2025:PHHC:000693 to Rs.300/- per day, as such I take the monthly income of the deceased as Rs.10,000/--..."
9.
It has further been argued by learned counsel for the appellants that nothing has been granted by way of consortium to the appellants.

However, a perusal of the impugned Award Award, especially Para 24 shows that the learned Tribunal has granted Rs.25,000/ Rs.25,000/- as funeral expenses;
Rs.1 lakh towards loss of love and affection affection; and additional Rs.1 lakh has been granted as loss of consortium to claimant No.1/widow.
From the above, it is clear that the appellant appellants have been granted consortium of 2 lakhs/- as opposed to entitl entitled sum of 1,92,000/--.

The learned Tribunal has further correctly applied deduction of 1/4th given the fact that there are four claimants; and as the deceased was only aged 53 years, multiplier of 11 has correctly been applied.
Furthermore, Furthermore, the appellants can derive no benefit from the relied upon judgment of Munna Lal Jain (supra) as the same is distinguishable on facts and law.
In the said case, the concerned High Court itself had determined income of the deceased therein to be Rs.12,000/-- per month and avocation of the deceased therein as Pandit was also proven on record.

10. In view of the above discussion, this appeal is allowed to the following extent: -
